questions: Does a 12 mm footprint at 12 mm spacing give clean, non-saturating readings on the line, or do multiple sensors read partial values that make the signal noisy?
Is the forward look-ahead of 0.04 m useful, or does it cause lag on tight bends that you would rather trade for a shorter offset?
Is wheel_track 0.12 m and mass 0.6 kg giving enough turn authority and stability at the speed needed to finish in 3 s?
Which sensor or edge positions are the limiting factor in slalom and s-bend tracks?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If the sensor span is wider than needed, or slalom bends cause line loss, propose a wider or more forward sensor array; report any problem with the sensor count.

intent: Establish a symmetric, evenly spaced five-sensor baseline with contiguous 12 mm footprints spanning the 25 mm tape, placed slightly ahead of the axle for look-ahead. Keep the body and wheel geometry mid-range and the mass low so the Integrator has a predictable platform to tune. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with the controller doing most of the work; the geometry is a reference point for later changes.
learning: Baseline from the contract only; no race evidence yet. Next iteration, revise geometry from the Integrator's sensing feedback and the race telemetry (rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation). Hypotheses to test: (1) 12 mm spacing with 12 mm footprints is adequate coverage; (2) a 0.04 m look-ahead reduces oscillation; (3) a lighter mass improves completion time without hurting stability.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or Integrator feedback, so this is a baseline built from the contract rather than from evidence. Five sensors at 12 mm spacing across x = -0.024 to +0.024 m keep the tape (25 mm wide) under at least one sensor footprint at any lateral offset within about the off-track limit, and the 12 mm footprint gives contiguous coverage with no blind gap. Placing them 0.04 m ahead of the axle gives the controller a look-ahead, so steering responds before the wheels reach the bend. A 0.12 m wheel track and 0.03 m wheel radius are mid-range, giving a moderate turn authority without excessive slip. Body width 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at its 0.06 m floor, since tape half-width plus a quarter body width (0.0425 m) is below it. Mass 0.6 kg is at the lower end to favour acceleration toward the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s. I expect a completed run on the oval, with line-loss events low because the sensor span covers the tape across small offsets; the main risk is sensor saturation on tight slalom bends.
